title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 56 (Transfer and Transmission of Securities)

content.overview: Section 56(1) provides that a company shall not register a transfer of securities of the company, or the interest of a member in a company having no share capital, other than a transfer between persons both of whose names are entered as holders of beneficial interest in the records of a depository, unless a proper instrument of transfer in the prescribed form, duly stamped, dated and executed by or on behalf of the transferor and the transferee and specifying the name, address and occupation, if any, of the transferee, has been delivered to the company by the transferor or the transferee within sixty days from the date of execution, along with the certificate relating to the securities or, if no such certificate is in existence, along with the letter of allotment. Where the instrument is lost or not delivered within the prescribed period, the company may register the transfer on such terms as to indemnity as the Board may think fit. Section 56(2) provides that nothing in sub-section (1) shall prejudice the power of the company to register, on receipt of an intimation of transmission of any right to securities by operation of law from any person to whom such right has been transmitted. Section 56(3) requires that where an application is made by the transferor alone and relates to partly paid shares, the transfer shall not be registered unless the company gives the prescribed notice to the transferee and the transferee gives no objection within two weeks of receipt of notice. Section 56(4) requires every company, unless prohibited by law or by order of Court, Tribunal or other authority, to deliver certificates of all securities allotted, transferred or transmitted within the specified periods (two months from incorporation for subscribers; two months from allotment for shares; one month from receipt of instrument or intimation for transfer/transmission; six months from allotment for debentures), with immediate intimation to the depository where securities are dealt with in a depository. Section 56(5) provides that a transfer of any security or other interest of a deceased person made by his legal representative shall, even if the legal representative is not a holder thereof, be valid as if he had been the holder at the time of execution of the instrument of transfer. Section 56(6) provides that where any default is made in complying with sub-sections (1) to (5), the company and every officer in default shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees. Section 56(7) provides that without prejudice to liability under the Depositories Act, 1996, where any depository or depository participant, with an intention to defraud a person, has transferred shares, it shall be liable under section 447.
content.glance: Proper instrument of transfer (prescribed form, stamped, dated, executed, delivered within 60 days with certificate) required for registration, except depository beneficial-interest transfers; transmission by operation of law without instrument; partly-paid transferor-alone applications need transferee no-objection; certificate delivery timelines; legal-representative transfers valid; default penalty ₹50,000; depository fraud attracts s. 447.
content.study: A company shall not register a transfer of securities of the company, or the interest of a member in the company in the case of a company having no share capital, other than the transfer between persons both of whose names are entered as holders of beneficial interest in the records of a depository, unless a proper instrument of transfer, in such form as may be prescribed, duly stamped, dated and executed by or on behalf of the transferor and the transferee and specifying the name, address and occupation, if any, of the transferee has been delivered to the company by the transferor or the transferee within a period of sixty days from the date of execution, along with the certificate relating to the securities, or if no such certificate is in existence, along with the letter of allotment of securities: Provided that where the instrument of transfer has been lost or the instrument of transfer has not been delivered within the prescribed period, the company may register the transfer on such terms as to indemnity as the Board may think fit (s. 56(1)). Nothing in sub-section (1) shall prejudice the power of the company to register, on receipt of an intimation of transmission of any right to securities by operation of law from any person to whom such right has been transmitted (s. 56(2)). Where an application is made by the transferor alone and relates to partly paid shares, the transfer shall not be registered, unless the company gives the notice of the application, in such manner as may be prescribed, to the transferee and the transferee gives no objection to the transfer within two weeks from the receipt of notice (s. 56(3)). Every company shall, unless prohibited by any provision of law or any order of Court, Tribunal or other authority, deliver the certificates of all securities allotted, transferred or transmitted—(a) within a period of two months from the date of incorporation, in the case of subscribers to the memorandum; (b) within a period of two months from the date of allotment, in the case of any allotment of any of its shares; (c) within a period of one month from the date of receipt by the company of the instrument of transfer under sub-section (1) or, as the case may be, of the intimation of transmission under sub-section (2), in the case of a transfer or transmission of securities; (d) within a period of six months from the date of allotment in the case of any allotment of debenture: Provided that where the securities are dealt with in a depository, the company shall intimate the details of allotment of securities to depository immediately on allotment of such securities (s. 56(4)). The transfer of any security or other interest of a deceased person in a company made by his legal representative shall, even if the legal representative is not a holder thereof, be valid as if he had been the holder at the time of the execution of the instrument of transfer (s. 56(5)). Where any default is made in complying with the provisions of sub-sections (1) to (5), the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees (s. 56(6)). Without prejudice to any liability under the Depositories Act, 1996, where any depository or depository participant, with an intention to defraud a person, has transferred shares, it shall be liable under section 447 (s. 56(7)). Current-law framing: classify transfer vs transmission; for transfer, test instrument, stamping, execution, delivery within 60 days, certificate or letter of allotment, and the depository exception; apply indemnity for lost/late instrument; for partly paid transferor-alone applications, apply the transferee notice and no-objection rule; apply the certificate delivery timelines; treat legal-representative transfers as valid under s. 56(5); apply the ₹50,000 penalty and s. 447 for depository fraud.

sections.heading: Transfer — instrument requirement (s. 56(1))
sections.body: Registration of transfer requires a proper prescribed instrument, duly stamped, dated and executed by or on behalf of transferor and transferee, specifying name, address and occupation of the transferee, delivered within sixty days of execution along with the certificate or letter of allotment. Exception: transfer between persons both entered as holders of beneficial interest in depository records. Lost or late instrument: Board may register on indemnity terms.

sections.heading: Transmission by operation of law (s. 56(2))
sections.body: Nothing in sub-section (1) prejudices the power of the company to register, on receipt of an intimation of transmission of any right to securities by operation of law from any person to whom such right has been transmitted.

sections.heading: Partly paid shares — transferor-alone application (s. 56(3))
sections.body: Where an application is made by the transferor alone and relates to partly paid shares, the transfer shall not be registered unless the company gives the prescribed notice to the transferee and the transferee gives no objection within two weeks from receipt of notice.

sections.heading: Certificate delivery timelines (s. 56(4))
sections.body: Unless prohibited by law or by order of Court, Tribunal or other authority: (a) two months from incorporation for subscribers to the memorandum; (b) two months from allotment for shares; (c) one month from receipt of instrument or intimation for transfer or transmission; (d) six months from allotment for debentures. Where securities are dealt with in a depository, intimate allotment details to the depository immediately on allotment.

sections.heading: Legal representative of deceased (s. 56(5))
sections.body: A transfer of any security or other interest of a deceased person made by his legal representative shall, even if the legal representative is not a holder thereof, be valid as if he had been the holder at the time of execution of the instrument of transfer.

sections.heading: Penalty and depository fraud (s. 56(6)–(7))
sections.body: Default in complying with sub-sections (1) to (5): company and every officer in default liable to a penalty of fifty thousand rupees. Depository or depository participant transferring shares with intention to defraud is liable under section 447, without prejudice to the Depositories Act, 1996.

examples.title: Valid transfer with instrument
examples.body: A duly stamped and executed prescribed transfer form is delivered with the share certificate within sixty days of execution. The company may register the transfer under s. 56(1).

examples.title: Transmission on death
examples.body: On the death of a member, the legal representative seeks registration by transmission. No instrument of transfer is required under s. 56(2). A transfer made by the legal representative is valid under s. 56(5) even if the representative is not a holder.

examples.title: Partly paid — transferor-alone application
examples.body: The transferor alone applies to register a transfer of partly paid shares. The company must give the prescribed notice to the transferee; registration may proceed only if the transferee gives no objection within two weeks (s. 56(3)).

hypotheticals.question: Is an oral agreement enough to compel registration of a share transfer?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 56(1) requires a proper instrument of transfer in the prescribed form, duly stamped, dated and executed, delivered with the certificate or letter of allotment within sixty days (subject to indemnity for loss or late delivery).

hypotheticals.question: Does transmission require an instrument of transfer?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 56(2) expressly preserves the power of the company to register on receipt of an intimation of transmission by operation of law, without the instrument requirements of sub-section (1).

distinctions.title: Transfer and transmission (s. 56) vs refusal of registration (s. 58)
distinctions.left: How transfer and transmission are effected; instrument, timelines and certificate delivery
distinctions.right: When registration may be refused and the Tribunal appeal route

misconceptions.trap: Transmission also needs a transfer form.
misconceptions.correction: Section 56(2) expressly preserves registration on intimation of transmission by operation of law without the instrument requirements of sub-section (1).

misconceptions.trap: All transfers require an instrument, including depository transfers.
misconceptions.correction: Section 56(1) excepts a transfer between persons both of whose names are entered as holders of beneficial interest in the records of a depository.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 56 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Classify the transaction as transfer or transmission. II. For transfer: test the depository exception; otherwise test prescribed instrument, stamping, execution, delivery within 60 days, certificate or letter of allotment; apply indemnity for lost/late instrument; for partly paid transferor-alone applications, apply s. 56(3) notice and no-objection. III. For transmission: apply s. 56(2) and, where relevant, s. 56(5) for legal representatives. IV. Check certificate delivery timelines under s. 56(4). V. Note the ₹50,000 penalty under s. 56(6) and s. 447 for depository fraud under s. 56(7). VI. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions on a Section 56 matter contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Classification as transfer or transmission; instrument facts (form, stamp, execution, delivery, certificate); depository status if relevant; partly-paid notice facts if relevant; transmission intimation and legal-representative capacity if relevant; certificate delivery timeline; precise relief; any penalty or s. 447 claim.

State the four certificate delivery timelines under s. 56(4).
Legal representative transfers are valid under s. 56(5).
Default penalty ₹50,000; depository fraud attracts s. 447.
